messages:
mira: Quick design review — the pool-switcher affordance in the Capacity modal is confusing, especially for keyboard/screen-reader flows. Currently we hide the GPU pool dropdown when Burst is enabled which makes it impossible to inspect or change the pool without toggling burst off. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/XXXX (see 'capacity/modal' frame). Thoughts? :eyes: devon: I ran into this while testing a Dedicated flow. Hiding = surprising. Could we show the dropdown disabled with an explanation tooltip instead of removing it? alex: Implementation note — our Dropdown component doesn't support a disabled+tooltip pattern out-of-the-box. We could render a read-only text input + icon button that opens the tooltip, which is easier than changing the shared dropdown. That keeps DOM order for a11y. mira: That sounds reasonable. Key requirements: 1) element must be focusable via keyboard, 2) it should expose aria-describedby pointing at the tooltip content, 3) visually indicate disabled state but still readable. Also the Min/Max steppers need proper labels — screen reader currently says "number input". Propose labels: 'Min GPUs' and 'Max GPUs' and helper text beneath each. Example copy: "Min GPUs — autoscaler lower bound." sara: Shorter copy suggestion for helper: 'Min GPUs — lower bound used by autoscaler.' For Max: 'Max GPUs — autoscaler upper bound.' Keep labels concise, move extra details to tooltip. kendall: A11y nits: helper text contrast is too low in the mock (approx 2.8:1). For small body text we need >=4.5:1 if it's primary info. If it's secondary maybe 3:1 is tolerable, but we should aim stronger. Also ensure steppers have visible focus rings and 44px touch targets. alex: Technically we already meet 44px for steppers. I'll add aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax and aria-label attributes. For the disabled-with-tooltip approach I'd do something like: ```
nv4-48
Pool is locked while Burst is enabled. Toggle Burst to change pool.
``` This keeps the element focusable and announces the tooltip via aria-describedby. mira: Nice. A couple copy tweaks: change label from 'Pool' to 'GPU pool' to be explicit. Tooltip copy idea: 'Pool is locked while Burst is enabled. Toggle Burst to change pool.' For the Burst control itself propose inline copy: 'Burst — temporarily allow capacity above Max for short spikes.' Tooltip: 'Burst increases capacity briefly; exceeded GPUs billed at premium rates.' sara: +1 to clearer labels. Also UX question: should enabling Burst collapse the Max control? My suggestion: don't collapse. Gray out Max and show a small 'Burst active' pill next to it. Hiding controls tends to confuse users. kendall: From a11y POV collapsing is bad. Live regions are helpful when values change. When the pool or burst state changes we should fire a polite live region like: "Selected GPU pool: nv4-48" or "Burst enabled" so screen readers get context without hunting. alex: I'll prototype the disabled-readonly input + tooltip and the live region announcements. If product confirms final copy I'll avoid adding new primitives. I can try to patch the existing Dropdown to support a readOnly prop but will do it as a small wrapper for now. mira: Cool — I'll update the Figma with the disabled-with-tooltip variant, stronger helper color, and the revised copy. Also adding a tiny accessibility note in the comments: 'aria-describedby -> tooltip id; announce pool changes via live region; steppers must set aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax.' sara: Copy lock: Labels: 'GPU pool', 'Min GPUs', 'Max GPUs'. Helper text: 'Min GPUs — lower bound used by autoscaler.' 'Max GPUs — upper bound used by autoscaler.' Burst tooltip: 'Burst increases capacity briefly; exceeded GPUs billed at premium rates.' kendall: I'll run a quick contrast check after Figma is updated. If you want I can also run a NVDA pass on the prototype. alex: Thanks — I'll send a short PR with the markup + notes tomorrow. mira: Thanks all! I'll post updated frames when done :thumbsup:
